title: Motion tween Ruffle visual oracle E2E (motion-tween.spec.ts)
description:
visual-oracle.spec.ts test 8 compares the authoring canvas at frame 2 against Ruffle at frame 0 — it never verifies that the compiled SWF actually positions the tween at the correct mid-frame location inside Ruffle. Shape morphs have a proper Ruffle oracle (shape-morph.spec.ts, task 0784) that times out at ~250 ms so Ruffle auto-plays to a mid-frame and asserts the shape changed. Motion tweens lack the equivalent.

Scope: add apps/desktop/e2e/motion-tween.spec.ts using the shape-morph.spec.ts pattern:

1. Build a 5-frame motion tween doc: a red 50×50 square starting at x=50 (frame 0) and ending at x=450 (frame 4), 12 fps.
2. Publish SWF via __flashTest.publish(), inject Ruffle player (same setup as shape-morph / button-roundtrip specs), load with autoplay:on.
3. Take a screenshot at t~0 ms (frame 0) — verify object is near x=50 (left side non-empty).
4. Wait ~250 ms (~3 frames at 12 fps), take another screenshot — verify object has moved rightward (pixel columns near x=50 are empty, columns near x=250 are non-empty).
5. Wait ~400 ms total, take a third screenshot — verify object is near x=450 (right side non-empty).
6. Test 2: oracle integrity check — a static (non-tween) doc must NOT move, confirming the oracle is a real runtime gate.

This is the first acceptance gate that proves compile.ts tween interpolation (PlaceObject2 move-flag frames) actually renders correctly in Ruffle at runtime — unit tests on SWF bytes are not sufficient per CLAUDE.md.

Acceptance: motion-tween.spec.ts: 2 tests pass locally (CI skip guard matching shape-morph.spec.ts).
